sentences.text:
And Another Counsel for Appellant :- Shankar Lal Pandey Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Arvind Kumar Tripathi Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
1.

Heard Shri Shankar Lal Pandey, learned counsel for the appellant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State, Shri Ujjwal Mishra holding brief of Shri Arvind Kumar Tripathi, learned counsel for the respondent no.2/victim/complainant and perused the record.

2. The instant criminal appeal under Section 14(A)(2) S.C./S.T. Act has been filed by the appellant/Ankur Sharma for grant of bail and to set-aside/quash the impugned order dated 14.05.2024 passed by the learned Special Judge (S.C./S.T. Act), Barabanki in Bail Application No.1387 of 2024, arising out of Case Crime No.60 of 2024, under Sections 323, 504, 506, 342, 376,
377, 328 I.P.C. and Section 3(1)(Da), 3(1)(Dha), 3(2)(v) of the S.C./S.T. Act, Police Station Satrikh,
District Barabanki, during trial.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant while pressing this appeal submits that the appellant has been falsely implicated in this case and he has not committed any offence as claimed by the prosecution.

1 4.

It is further submitted that the F.I.R., which has been lodged by none other than the victim/prosecutrix herself, would evidently reveal that the prosecutrix was having an affair with the appellant and she had accompanied the appellant on 05.12.2023, the day on which her 'vidai'
ceremony was scheduled to be solemnized and thereafter had remained with him for about two months and the age of the victim at the relevant point of time was more than 30 years, therefore, the prosecutrix was major and had accompanied the appellant on her own, which may not attract any offence.

5. It is further submitted that it is also admitted to the prosecutrix that the appellant and she were in a relationship for about three years from before lodging of the F.I.R. and in the F.I.R. there is no allegation with regard to the blackmailing on the basis of any obscene photograph or video,
however, the prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. has stated that she was being blackmailed by the appellant on the basis of some photographs and videos,
however, she maintained in her statement recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. that she had gone in the morning of 05.12.2023 at about 05:00am. to meet the appellant.

6. It is vehemently submitted that the prosecutrix was in a relationship with the appellant and they have decided to solemnize marriage and it is on this pretext, the prosecutrix had accompanied the appellant and therefore, the allegations of her abduction as levelled in the F.I.R. may not be believed by any prudent person.

It is also submitted that the story of confinement of the prosecutrix at Manas place is also not corroborated by any evidence as the owner/manager of the hostel, where appellant was living, has not stated that the prosecutrix was confined in the room, which was given on rent to the appellant.

7. It is also submitted that the story of making sexual relations on the pretext of false promise of marriage is also after thought and keeping in view the fact that the prosecutrix is aged about more than 30 years, it is hard to digest that she may be lured at this age on the pretext of marrying, thus it is evident that the relations between the appellant and the prosecutrix were the relationship of two adults and may not attract any penal provision and the allegations of rape are not substantiated by any medical evidence.
8. It is also submitted that appellant is in jail in this case since 09.03.2024 and he is not having any criminal antecedents.
Charge sheet in this case has already been submitted and there is no apprehension that after being released on bail the appellant may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.

9. Learned A.G.A. as well as Shri Ujjwal Mishra holding brief of Shri Arvind Kumar Tripathi, learned counsel for the respondent no.2/victim/complainant vehemently opposes the prayer of bail of the appellant on the ground that it is not only a case where the sexual relations were made for a long time on the pretext of marrying with the victim by the appellant, but also she has been abducted and was kept in confinement and was constantly sexually abused for about two months and having regard to the material/evidence available against the appellant, he is not entitled to be released on bail, but could not controvert the other factual submissions made by learned counsel for the appellant.

2 10.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is evident that age of the prosecutrix at the relevant point of time was more than 30 years, thus she at the relevant point of time was a major girl.

She has admitted in the F.I.R. that she at first met with the appellant at the house of her maternal grandmother about three years ago from before lodging of the F.I.R.
and was in a relationship with the appellant since then.

The allegations of making sexual relations on the pretext of extending false promise of marriage has also been levelled and also that on 05.12.2023 when 'vidai' ceremony of the prosecutrix was scheduled to be solemnized, she had gone to meet the appellant from where she was abducted and was kept in confinement.

It has been submitted with considerable force by learned counsel for the appellant that the day, which has been chosen by the prosecutrix to meet the appellant, was the day on which her 'vidai' ceremony was scheduled to be solemnized and this fact alone is sufficient to infer that the appellant and the prosecutrix have conjointly planned to escape.

Significantly the owner/manager of the hostel, where the appellant was living at the relevant point of time, has also not corroborated the fact of confinement of the prosecutrix in the room of appellant as alleged by the prosecutrix in her statement.

In the F.I.R., there is no mention about filming of any photograph or video, which has been shown the basis of blackmailing in the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
Charge-sheet in this case has already been filed.
Appellant is in jail in this case since 09.03.2024 without any previous criminal history.
The presence of the appellant could be secured before the trial court by placing adequate conditions.

11. Having regard to all the facts and circumstances of the case, in the considered opinion of this Court, the trial court has erred materially in passing the impugned order and same is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly the impugned order dated14.05.2024 passed by the court below is set-aside and the appeal filed by the appellant is allowed.
Pending application(s) stand disposed of.

12. Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, let the appellant- Ankur Sharma involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The appellant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The appellant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The appellant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
13.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
14. Identity, status and residence proof of the appellant and sureties be verified by the Court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
